newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PRICE AND NORMAN LEAD KEMPER OPEN AFTER ONE ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRICE AND NORMAN LEAD KEMPER OPEN AFTER ONE ROUND.

text.p: Nick Price and Greg Norman, two of the heavyweights of world golf, shared the lead after the opening round at the $1.5 million Kemper Open on Thursday.

Price, displaying ominously-good form before next week's U.S. Open, parred every hole on the front nine, then stormed home with five back nine birdies to join friend and rival Norman at five-under-par 66 at the Avenel TPC course.
They were one stroke ahead of Jeff Sluman, Kelly Gibson and Paul Stankowski, while British Open champion Tom Lehman was among six players two shots back.
"On the front nine I hit the ball really well. I just didn't make any putts," said Florida-based Zimbabwean Price.
"I was getting a little frustrated (but) my putting kicked in on the back nine. That helped me to be more aggressive with my iron play.
"I drove it super today," added Price, who took off the past two weeks off to rest tendinitis in his right hand.
"I've had the problem for 16 or 17 years and it comes and goes," he said.
"During the (Byron Nelson Classic three weeks ago) it didn't hurt really badly but I could feel it. That's a warning signal to take some time off."
Norman got off to a dream start with an eagle at the par-five second, where he holed out with a pitching wedge from 126 yards.

The Australian star added five birdies and two bogeys in a continuation of the good form he showed in finishing tied for second Monday at the Memorial tournament, where he was deprived of a chance at victory when the scheduled fourth round was cancelled.

"Either I'm happy this is the first round of the Kemper or I wish it was the fourth round of Memorial," quipped a relaxed Norman, the world's top-ranked player -- ahead of Tiger Woods, for the time being at least.

"I'm pretty happy with the way I played. I hit a lot of fairways and a lot of greens. I'm not worried about the U.S. Open right now. I'm more concerned about putting in a great performance this week."
Norman outplayed Briton Nick Faldo, with whom he was paired. Three-time Masters champion Faldo started double-bogey, bogey on his way to an inconsistent 73.
"I was looking forward to today and I started six, six," lamented Faldo, who dusted off Norman in a head-to-head showdown at last year's Masters final round.
"I was very disappointed. It wasn't very good. There's plenty to work on."
